narr: A big push of monsoon moisture led to ten days of scattered thunderstorms over the Mojave Desert. Many storms produced flash flooding and/or high winds. Events in this episode are continued in the July 22-26 Thunderstorms episode.
ev: Spencer Drive in Meadview was flooded and covered with mud.
At least three roads were closed, at least one home was inundated, and major flooding occurred inside the park, impacting several campground cabins.
Two feet of water flooded Temple Bar Road.
Two to three feet of water flooded DW Ranch Road from 1225 to 1330, and again from 1425 to 1600.
Water and debris flowed over Aztec Road and Bacobi Road near Shinarump Drive.
Water flowed over Stockton Hill Road.
lsr: SPOTTER IN MEADVIEW REPORTED THAT WATER WASHED OUT SPENCER DRIVE AND LEFT QUITE A BIT OF MUD OVER THE ROAD. ALSO REPORTED THAT THE WASH HAD CROSSED OVER PIERCE FERRY ROAD YESTERDAY.
EMERGENCY MANAGEMENT REPORTS FLASH FLOODING ACROSS HUALAPAI MOUNTAIN ROAD AT DEVILS DIP. WATER APPEARS TO BE 2-3 FEET DEEP AND FLOWING VERY FAST.
FLASH FLOODING IS OCCURRING AT HUALAPAI PARK WITH A SECOND ROUND OF HEAVY RAIN. EMERGENCY MANAGER REPORTS THAT LIFE THREATENING IS OCCURRING INSIDE THE PARK NEAR SUMMER CAMP.
